title: COLR3: prefix collimation with fixed-group malformed-copy tolerance

claims.statement: For COLR3 in proof.md and its reproduced base-proof.md, label-tools.md and gradient-tools.md, for every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ let n=ceil(log2 N), K=32(n+1), and Q0=N(n+2) for n<4096 or the literal COL4 Qcap for n>=4096. Run the complete bounded COL4 independently K times, padding each group with discarded source acquisitions to exactly Q0 before starting the next, and return a strict majority answer or zero. The actual acquired count on every branch is Q=K Q0. Under the fixed-position joint malformed-copy model below with at most n malformed copies in the ENTIRE run, unconditional full-secret success is greater than 63/64, including clean input. On every execution branch the SAME program has total charged sequential work T=O(n^(35/2) 2^((286/63)sqrt n)), jointly with all other bounds and the original count tolerance. All outside constants are absolute; the fixed finite prefix is fully specified. The supported envelope has exact growth index 1/2. Every padding copy, discarded attempt, reset, source/work abort, parameter computation, lookup, gate/address/controller step and temporary allocation is charged in the evidence.

structured.error_model: Among Q acquired source copies, at most tau(n,Q) positions fixed before the algorithm private randomness may contain an arbitrary joint state on their declared source registers. Every other copy is an independent ideal coset state for the same fixed secret s; their product state is independent of the malformed subsystem. The adversary may know N,s and the algorithm but cannot alter the controller or registers after delivery. Malformed copies may be mutually entangled. The algorithm is not told the malformed positions.
